folder: Clinical Medicine and Surgery I Exam 8

items.html: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism, so remember venous thromboembolism prophylaxis for inpatients, and consider it in outpatients.

src.question: A 64-year-old man is admitted with autoimmune hemolytic anemia confirmed by a positive direct antiglobulin test. He is hemodynamically stable with hemoglobin 8.1 g/dL (normal 13.5-17.5 g/dL), and glucocorticoids have been started. Which order should also be part of his admission?
src.explanation: Correct. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism, so remember venous thromboembolism prophylaxis for inpatients, and consider it in outpatients. As an inpatient with this disease he should have it ordered.

items.section_title: 1.22 · Hemoglobin C, fetal hemoglobin and sickle cell management
items.html: Preventing infection in sickle cell disease. Sickle cell disease brings increased susceptibility to encapsulated bacteria, so prevention is vaccinations, indicated childhood penicillin prophylaxis and infection education.

src.question: A 2-year-old girl with sickle cell disease is seen for a well-child visit. Her parents ask what can prevent serious infections, since children with her disease are susceptible to encapsulated bacteria. Which preventive plan is indicated?
src.explanation: Correct. Sickle cell disease brings increased susceptibility to encapsulated bacteria, so prevention is vaccinations, indicated childhood penicillin prophylaxis and infection education. Prevention and emergency care vary with age, genotype and clinical history.

items.html: Education after an attack. Education for this deficiency is to avoid oxidative triggers and seek care for jaundice or dark urine, the signs of an acute hemolytic attack. With trigger avoidance the prognosis is usually favorable.

src.question: A 22-year-old man recovered from an episode of hemolysis triggered by fava beans, and a low glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level later confirmed the deficiency. Which instruction should be part of his education?
src.explanation: Correct. Education for this deficiency is to avoid oxidative triggers and seek care for jaundice or dark urine, the signs of an acute hemolytic attack. With trigger avoidance the prognosis is usually favorable.
